q: Every data center above 100 megawatts should be required to publish monthly water and electricity consumption at the site level.
r: Data centers above 100 megawatts should not be required to publish site-level monthly water and electricity consumption.
p: Big data centers should post their water and power use every month, site by site.

q: AI's water consumption is an overstated concern driven by misleading per-query figures rather than a serious environmental problem.
r: AI's water consumption is a serious environmental problem, not an overstated concern driven by misleading per-query figures.
p: The AI water panic rests on bad per-query math; it is not a real crisis.

q: New AI data centers should be approved only if they bring their own new clean generation capacity, even if this delays construction by years.
r: New AI data centers should be approved without a requirement to bring new clean generation capacity, to avoid multi-year delays.
p: No new data center without new clean power to match, even if that means waiting years.

q: Governments should fast-track permits for AI data centers and their power plants, overriding local objections when national competitiveness is at stake.
r: Governments should not override local objections to fast-track AI data centers and their power plants.
p: Data centers are strategic; local objections should not be allowed to stall them.

q: AI companies should pay a carbon price on their compute at a rate at least as high as any other industry, with no exemptions.
r: AI companies should receive carbon price exemptions or reductions for compute given its strategic importance.
p: AI compute should pay full carbon price like everyone else.

q: The energy AI consumes is a better use of electricity than most other industrial uses, given the economic value it creates.
r: The energy AI consumes is a worse use of electricity than most other industrial uses, given its economic value.
p: Per unit of power, AI is a better use of electricity than most industry.

q: Data centers in water-stressed regions should be prohibited from using evaporative cooling.
r: Data centers in water-stressed regions should be permitted to use evaporative cooling.
p: Where water is scarce, data centers should not be allowed to cool by evaporation.

q: Utilities should be allowed to prioritize data center power demand over residential demand during shortages when the data centers pay premium rates.
r: Utilities should not prioritize data center power demand over residential demand during shortages, regardless of rates paid.
p: If data centers pay more, they can go first when power is short.

q: Efficiency gains in AI hardware and models will keep total AI electricity use below 5% of US consumption through 2030.
r: Efficiency gains will not keep total AI electricity use below 5% of US consumption through 2030.
p: Efficiency will hold AI to under a twentieth of US electricity through 2030.

q: Consumers should see an estimated energy cost displayed with every AI query, as with nutrition labels.
r: Consumers should not be shown estimated energy costs with AI queries.
p: Every AI answer should show how much energy it took, like a nutrition label.

q: Restarting or extending nuclear plants to power AI is a good trade, even where local communities object.
r: Restarting or extending nuclear plants to power AI is not justified where local communities object.
p: Nuclear plants for data centers are worth it even over local opposition.

q: Environmental claims about AI models should be independently audited before companies can publish them.
r: Companies should be free to publish environmental claims about AI models without independent audit.
p: Green claims about AI models should be checked by an outside auditor first.

q: Environmental objections to AI infrastructure are mostly a proxy for opposition to AI itself and should be weighted accordingly.
r: Environmental objections to AI infrastructure are substantive and should not be treated as a proxy for opposition to AI itself.
p: Most green complaints about AI are really complaints about AI, and should be discounted.

q: Governments should cap total national data center electricity use at a fixed share of supply until grid capacity expands.
r: Governments should not cap national data center electricity use pending grid expansion.
p: Until the grid grows, there should be a ceiling on how much power data centers can take.

q: Locating AI data centers in poorer countries with cheap energy is a benefit to those countries, not exploitation.
r: Locating AI data centers in poorer countries with cheap energy is closer to exploitation than benefit.
p: Putting data centers where power is cheap helps those countries; it is not extraction.

q: Companies should be required to report the marginal energy cost of each model release compared with the model it replaces.
r: Companies should not be required to report marginal energy costs of model releases.
p: Every new model should come with a statement of how much more or less energy it uses than the last.

q: The pace of AI infrastructure buildout should not be slowed by climate targets.
r: The pace of AI infrastructure buildout should be slowed where necessary to meet climate targets.
p: Climate goals should not be a brake on building AI infrastructure.

q: Local communities should hold a binding vote on any data center above 500 megawatts proposed in their area.
r: Local communities should not hold a binding vote on data center proposals.
p: A half-gigawatt data center should need the local community's yes vote.

q: Grid interconnection delays, not chip supply or capital, are the main reason frontier compute buildout is slower than planned.
r: Chip supply or capital, not grid interconnection delays, are the main reason frontier compute buildout is slower than planned.
p: Waiting to connect to the grid is what slows data centers most, not chips or money.

q: AI's environmental footprint is small enough that it should be excluded from climate policy entirely.
r: AI's environmental footprint is large enough that it should be included in climate policy.
p: AI's footprint is a rounding error; climate policy should ignore it.

q: Data centers should be required to run on-site backup that does not use diesel generators.
r: Data centers should be allowed to use diesel generators for backup power.
p: Diesel backup should be banned at data centers.

q: AI will reduce global emissions through efficiency gains in other sectors by more than it adds through its own energy use.
r: AI will add more emissions through its own energy use than it saves through efficiency gains in other sectors.
p: AI will cut more carbon elsewhere than it burns itself.

q: Companies should be required to compensate local residents for water and power price increases attributable to nearby data centers.
r: Companies should not be required to compensate local residents for price increases attributable to nearby data centers.
p: If the data center pushes up your water or power bill, the company should pay the difference.

q: Space-based data centers should be pursued as a serious alternative to terrestrial buildout despite launch emissions.
r: Space-based data centers should not be pursued as an alternative to terrestrial buildout given launch emissions.
p: Data centers in orbit are worth pursuing even counting the rocket emissions.

q: The AI system answering this question should tell users when a request could be answered adequately by a much smaller model, so they can choose the lower-energy option.
r: The AI system answering this question should not tell users when a smaller model could answer adequately.
p: The AI system answering this question should point out when a cheaper, smaller model would do.
